title: Sensex Ends 319 Points Lower, Nifty At 25,144 As Inflation Breaches RBI Limit
excerpt: Benchmarks snapped a three-day winning run on November 13 as October inflation at 6.09% and crude above $95 a barrel weighed on auto, realty and metal stocks.
body:
• The Sensex closed 318.56 points, or 0.39%, lower at 81,592.45 on Friday, November 13, and the Nifty fell 155.05 points, or 0.61%, to 25,144.30, ending a three-day winning run.
  • October retail inflation rose to 6.09%, above the RBI's 6% upper tolerance limit, while crude traded above $95 a barrel - the two drivers sources named for the fall.
  • India VIX fell 6.45% to 15.55, and Shriram Finance was the top Nifty loser, down 3.37%; despite Friday's fall, both benchmarks still gained for the week.
  • Reader utility: foreign investors bought Rs 7,830.60 crore net on Thursday while domestic institutions sold Rs 6,331.17 crore - check that flow split before reading Friday's fall as a trend break.

Indian benchmarks ended a three-day winning run on Friday, November 13. The BSE Sensex closed down 318.56 points, or 0.39%, at 81,592.45, and the NSE Nifty fell 155.05 points, or 0.61%, to settle at 25,144.30, according to closing data reported by Upstox and BusinessLine.

What drove the decline

Sources named two pressures. India's retail inflation climbed to 6.09% in October, breaching the Reserve Bank of India's upper tolerance limit of 6% for the first time in two years, up from 5.54% in September. BusinessLine reported economists anticipating a policy rate hike by the central bank next month in response. Crude oil added to the concern: prices traded above $95 a barrel in the afternoon, with an intraday high of $96.76, as investors reacted to comments by US President Donald Trump that he would not hesitate to resume military strikes on Iran, Upstox reported.

Selling was broad. The Nifty touched an intraday low of 25,054.40 and the Sensex 81,288.75 before buying at lower levels trimmed losses into the close. Market breadth favoured declines: of 3,721 stocks traded on the NSE, 1,446 advanced and 2,179 declined. The total market capitalisation of BSE-listed companies fell by about Rs 2.1 lakh crore to Rs 510.17 lakh crore, Moneycontrol's wrap reported via TradingView.

Sectors and stocks

All sectoral indices ended in the red on the NSE, led by Realty, down 1.39% on Upstox's measure, followed by Auto at -1.07%, Metal at -0.98%, Private Bank at -0.76% and IT at -0.72%. Moneycontrol put auto, realty and metal each down around 1%. Broader markets fell less: the Nifty Midcap 100 lost 0.24% to 61,889.50 and the Smallcap 100 lost 0.26% to 19,656.45.

Among Nifty stocks, Shriram Finance fell 3.37%, Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles 3.31%, Grasim Industries 2.60%, Hindalco Industries 2.12% and Adani Enterprises 1.95%. Gainers included Eicher Motors, up 1.34%, BSE, up 0.73%, Asian Paints, up 0.53%, and Bharti Airtel, up 0.48%. On the Sensex, Mahindra & Mahindra, UltraTech Cement, Bharat Electronics, NTPC, Trent and HDFC Bank were among the laggards, while Hindustan Unilever, Asian Paints, Bharti Airtel and Reliance Industries were among the winners, BusinessLine reported.

Currency, volatility and the week

The rupee weakened for a second session. Moneycontrol reported a close of 94.24 per US dollar, down 21 paise from 94.03, while BusinessLine's provisional interbank report put the settle at 94.20, down 8 paise; the two reports reflect provisional versus closing prints and point the same way. India VIX, the volatility gauge, fell 6.45% to 15.55, suggesting options traders were not pricing a sharper fall. For the week, the Sensex added 0.7% and the Nifty 0.45%, so Friday's decline trimmed, rather than erased, a third consecutive weekly gain.
